Lessons.Title: Problems About Perimeter and Area
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will apply what you know about multiplication and division to convert units of measurement and solve multi-step problems involving perimeter and area.
This lesson prompts you to apply your reasoning skills and knowledge of all operations to solve problems about area and perimeter. Along the way, you also use multiplication and division to convert units of measurement. Most numbers used here are two- and three-digit numbers.

Source activity sequence: Warm-up: How Many Do You See: Shaded Squares (10 minutes); Activity 1: Create a Class Banner (15 minutes); Activity 2: Replace the Classroom Carpet (20 minutes); Cool-down: Paper for a Banner (5 minutes)
Exact mathematical focus: Use consistent length units: area = length × width and perimeter is the sum of all outside sides.

Edulytics authored model: 36 in × 24 in = 864 in² of poster area. 8 ft = 96 in, so 8 in × 96 in = 768 in² of banner area. The area comparison supports enough paper; cutting and rearrangement require a real construction check.
First-party Cool-down: Find the area and perimeter of a 12-ft by 8-ft room.
Original diagrams, live construction, classroom response, and publisher login-gated Cool-down are not digitally certified.
